reading: Four scattered 3x3 objects of one colour are gathered into a 7x7 grid as a 2x2 layout with a one-cell gap, each object keeping its shape and going to the quadrant matching its relative position (top/bottom, left/right).

slots.subject: the four 3x3 objects (8-connected components)
slots.layout: 7x7 canvas, quadrants at (0,0),(0,4),(4,0),(4,4) separated by a blank row/column
slots.order: quadrant chosen by the object's relative vertical and horizontal position among the four

why: each output quadrant equals exactly one input object's 3x3 box, in the same relative arrangement

reading: The colour-1 shape on top has downward-open cavities; every colour-5 piece below that could be slid up (rotation allowed) to completely fill one cavity is recoloured 2, the others stay 5.
verb: recolour pieces that fit the lock

slots.lock: the colour-1 object; its cavities are background pockets bounded by 1 on the sides and top, open at the bottom
slots.subject: colour-5 pieces (8-connected components)
slots.test: piece, in some rotation, covers all cells of one cavity without overlapping colour 1 (extra cells may stick out below)

why: exactly the 5-pieces that can exactly fill some cavity of the 1-shape change to 2; nothing else changes

reading: Each single coloured cell moves to the nearest 2x2 block of 5 and parks in the cell of the block's surrounding ring on its side (touching the block, edge or corner); the blocks stay.

new_rows.name: dot
new_rows.datalog:
osize(O, count(Y, X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
dot(Y, X) :- obj(O, Y, X), osize(O, N), N = 1.

why: every dot keeps its colour and ends 8-adjacent to its nearest 5-block; nothing else changes

reading: Two markers (one in the top half, one in the bottom half) each draw, in their own colour, the outline of their half of the grid (top row/bottom row and both side columns) plus a full horizontal line through the marker's row.

slots.subject: the two marker cells
slots.region: top half rows 0-4 for the upper marker, bottom half rows 5-9 for the lower
slots.pattern: left and right border columns of the half, the grid's outer row in that half, and the full row through the marker, all in the marker's colour

why: every output cell of the half is marker colour exactly on its side columns, outer row and marker row

reading: A 3x3 multicoloured block shoots a ray from each of its 8 outer cells outward (edge cells straight, corner cells diagonally) in that cell's colour to the grid border; the centre cell emits nothing.
why: each ray continues the cell's direction from the block centre and reaches the border

reading: The grid is 3x3 panels cut by separator lines; the shape in the top-left panel is the template, and in every panel the template positions that are empty are filled with the separator colour, existing cells kept.

new_rows.name: gap
new_rows.datalog:
tmpl(Y0, X0) :- cell(Y0, X0, C), Y0 < 5, X0 < 5.
rowof(Y, Y0) :- tmpl(Y0, X0), Y = Y0.
rowof(Y, Y0) :- tmpl(Y0, X0), px(Y, X0, C), Y = Y0 + 6.
rowof(Y, Y0) :- tmpl(Y0, X0), px(Y, X0, C), Y = Y0 + 12.
colof(X, X0) :- tmpl(Y0, X0), X = X0.
colof(X, X0) :- tmpl(Y0, X0), px(Y0, X, C), X = X0 + 6.
colof(X, X0) :- tmpl(Y0, X0), px(Y0, X, C), X = X0 + 12.
gap(Y, X) :- tmpl(Y0, X0), rowof(Y, Y0), colof(X, X0), px(Y, X, C), !cell(Y, X, C).

why: every background cell at a template position (period 6) becomes the separator colour; nothing else changes

reading: Each L-tromino casts a copy of itself shifted one cell diagonally onto background: colour-5 Ls shift into their inner corner and paint 4, colour-2 Ls shift away from their corner and paint 3 (3 wins on overlap).

slots.subject: each L-tromino (3-cell object)
slots.offset: one diagonal step; toward the bend's open side for 5, opposite for 2
slots.rest: only background cells are painted; originals kept

why: every new cell is a shifted cell of an L, coloured by the L's colour; nothing else changes

reading: A 2x2 block with some red (2) cells slides diagonally toward each red corner to the border, leaving a 2-wide diagonal band in the block's other colour; the block itself becomes that colour.

slots.subject: the 2x2 block
slots.directions: one diagonal per red cell, from the block centre through that cell

why: every swept position of the block is filled with the main colour, nothing else

reading: The 3x3 input is scaled by 2; each 5 cell becomes the 2x2 pattern 12/21 and each background cell a 2x2 background block.
why: output block (i,j) is the pattern iff input cell (i,j) is foreground

reading: Three 3x3 coloured blocks sit on top, with a key row below each block giving a marker colour; the output is the area below the separator, where every marker is replaced by the block keyed to its colour, centred on the marker, on background 7.

slots.legend: the three 3x3 blocks in rows 0-2, each paired with the marker colour found under it in row 4
slots.canvas: the panel below the full separator row (13x11)
slots.anchors: the marker cells in that panel
slots.unit: the block whose key colour equals the marker's colour, centred on the marker

why: each 3x3 block in the output is centred on a lower-panel marker and matches that marker's legend block
